main_text.p: juris, & sicut gubernatio populi per potentiam regiam non est de scientia religionis gradu primo, verum determinatum quid sine quo non perficitur religio, eodem modo se habet, scientia rationis gubernandi, &c. Porro, quod de arcta ista inter الدنيا Mundum, الملك Regnum, & الدين Religionem, necessitudine ita ut vix separatim consistere possint, affirmat, consonum est illi quod tradit Apostolus, 1 Tim, 2. 2. jubens orationes fieri, Pro Regibus, & omnibus qui in sublimitate constituti sunt; ut quietam & tranquillam vitam agamus. Quadrant & Hebraeorum antiquiorum sententiae, illa inprimis R. Chanina, הוי מתפלל בשלומה של מלכות , Pirke Abotb. c. 3.§.2. Ores pro pace regni, quoniam nisi timor sit, homines se invicem deglutient vivos, nec non illa R. Eleezeri, אם אין תורה אין דרך ארץ אין דרך ארץ אין תורה &c. Si non sit lex non est via terra, si non sit via terra non est lex, & si non sit farina non est lex, si non sit lex non est farina, §. 17. يرى بذلك ان كل واحد منهما مفيد في وجود Innuit hoc dicto الآخر وتتم (inquit Maimonides in Comment:) alteram harum rerum ad alterius τὸ [illegible, ~3 letters] conducere, eamque perficere. Quanta autem sit mutua haec inter regem & populum dependentia, sedulo olim populo ut inculcarent caviffe videntur Persarum reges instituto eum in finem festo, quo كان الملك ينزل عن سرير الملك ويلبس الثياب البيض ويرفع الحجاب ويترك هيبة الملك وينظر في مصالح الناس ويخاطبه[?] كل من شاء من الوضيع

page.notes: Long s rendered as plain s throughout. Arabic and Hebrew transcribed from the scan; the Arabic line ending "ويخاطبه" and the Hebrew of the Eleazar quotation are doubtful and were not fully verified. The Greek word after "ad alterius" is only partly legible. The Arabic line before "Innuit hoc dicto" and the phrase "الآخر وتتم" are partly legible and may be misordered. The italic/roman distinction in some Latin words (e.g., "Maimonides", "in Comment:") is approximate. The printed text starts mid-sentence and continues onto the next page.
